content:
As the WhatsApp username feature is about to officially launch, the app now allows users to record usernames, names, and phone numbers when saving contacts. Details below.

The new contact addition feature with a username field is gradually rolling out to some WhatsApp users

While the username feature has long been standard on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun moving away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp began rolling out its username reservation system earlier this year, allowing users to register their preferred usernames ahead of the feature's official launch to prevent identity impersonation by scammers.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has started adding a username field when users add new contacts. This field is positioned between the last name field and the phone number field.

Source: WABetaInfo

WABetaInfo pointed out that the username field appears to be gradually rolling out to selected users on both the WhatsApp beta and stable versions.

When the author tested using the latest stable version, although the field was displayed, the system still showed a message saying "This username is not on WhatsApp" even when the entered username did exist.

Nevertheless, this marks another step forward for WhatsApp as it gradually catches up with its competitors, adding a basic feature that many believe should have been in place long ago.
